title: MXB Facts card
description: One card: one release of one tool. The build (site/build.py) checks every card against this schema, then against the rules in rules/template.md and rules/questions.md: it sets the scores and key-question marks itself.

tool.description: The tool's name, as its author names it

summary.description: Two short sentences shown under the name on the tool's page, written from the analysis

header.description: The header rows of rules/template.md, by label, except Files checked (see files). Each game the Game row names brings its mods site's row: "mxb-mods.com" for MX Bikes, "gpb-mods.com" for GP Bikes

What it is.description: What the tool is and where it goes, in two or three sentences, from the analysis

In one line.description: What the tool is and does, at most 90 characters, written from the analysis: never the author's own claims and no words that judge. Shown under the tool's name

Category.description: It says what kind of tool it is, so readers can find similar ones; it says nothing about the tool's quality

Author.description: The name the author publishes as their public identity (GitHub name, the name on its licence or page)

Game.description: One or both of: MX Bikes; GP Bikes, in that order. The PiBoSo games the release shows it is made for: a plugin or setting for that game in its files, or code that reads that game's folders, never only the author's word. Each game named is run in its demo, or a Limits line says it wasn't

mxb-mods.com.description: For a tool whose Game row names MX Bikes: its mxb-mods.com page, "None found", or "Not checked" with the reason

gpb-mods.com.description: For a tool whose Game row names GP Bikes: its gpb-mods.com page, "None found", or "Not checked" with the reason

GitHub.description: Its GitHub repository or releases, or "None found"

Received as.description: Only for a file sent to us: what was received and where it came from

Held back.description: Only while an item is held back under rule 9: "<n> item(s) (rule 9): <question IDs>". Those answers can't be Good. The dates (when the author was told, and the end, 30 days later at most) are kept privately by the maintainer, not in the repository

Licence clause.description: Only when the licence forbids the analysis (rule 6): the clause, quoted, with a link to it or the SHA-256 of the file it is in. A card has this row if, and only if, an answer is "Not allowed"; that card gets "Not scored" in place of a score. A clause added in a later release applies from that release on; a card for an earlier release stays (rule 2)

Earlier reports.description: Only when the tool has earlier cards: a link to each, newest first, as `[<version>](https://thomas4f.github.io/mxb-facts/<tool>/<version>/)`, so a reader can see what changed between releases. The newest card is the tool's page; each earlier one keeps its page and badges at that address

Method.description: That the analysis was done by an AI assistant, and the model and effort it ran with; read the source at the commit; compared release files to source where possible; what was and wasn't run

files.description: File names + SHA-256 of what players download, and of the files inside them that were checked (the `files` list)

name.description: File name as shipped; "Zip" for an unnamed download

inside.description: The listed file this one comes from

files_note.description: What else the header says about the files (code signing, matching published hashes)

key.description: Short answers to the ten key questions: a few words, then the detail. No mark: the build sets it

areas.description: One line per area on what the tool does there, from the analysis; the area's score comes from the answers' costs

sections.description: The report sections of rules/template.md, in order, each a list of paragraphs, lists and tables

enum: What it says vs what it does

answers.description: One answer per question in rules/questions.md, by its ID (the build checks that none is missing or unknown)

by_maintainer.description: Only on a card of a tool made by the person who runs MXB Facts: the tool's page then shows a notice saying so, with the Author row (see README, "Conflict of interest")

corrections.description: Comments on answers sent through the "Comment on an answer" form (GitHub issues), oldest first: a correction, something missing, or context from the tool's author. While a correction or something missing is open, each answer it names shows its count on the comment icon, and the tool a neutral "under review" tag; nothing else on the card changes until it is decided. The author's context marks no answer

issue.description: The issue number in this repository

kind.description: What it is: a correction (the answer is wrong or out of date), something missing, or context from the tool's author. Left out, it is a correction

questions.description: The questions the comment itself names. A correction or something missing names at least one; the author's context may name none, and marks no answer either way

status.description: fixed: the card changed (a Card history row links the issue); declined: it doesn't hold; noted: answered without a change to the card (usually context)

reason.description: Once decided: what was fixed, or why it was declined, in one line

history.description: Card history, oldest first, one change per row

questions.description: A Concern line or row only: the answers it backs; it is shown as a Concern when one of them is

oneOf.description: Limits of this analysis only: each thing we couldn't prove or run, with the questions whose answers it affects (none when it touches no single question)

questions.description: A Concern line or row only: the answers it backs; it is shown as a Concern when one of them is

Verdict.description: What it says vs what it does only: the verdict on one claim, which may add words after its own ("Matches, as far as checked")
